arxiv-2109-04189.title: Eigenspectra of solar active region long-period oscillations
arxiv-2109-04189.creator: G. Dumbadze, B.M. Shergelashvili, S. Poedts, T.V. Zaqarashvili, M. Khodachenko, and P. De Causmaecker
arxiv-2109-04189.description: Abstract Context. We studied the low-frequency ≲ 0.5 \lesssim 0.5\; h -1 (long-period ≳ 2 \gtrsim 2\; h) oscillations of active regions (ARs). The investigation is based on an analysis of a time series built from Solar Dynamics Observatory/Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager (SDO/HMI) photospheric magnetograms and comprises case studies of several types of AR structures. Aims.

arxiv-2112-14122.title: A connection between symmetry breaking for Sobolev minimizers and stationary Navier-Stokes flows past a circular obstacle
arxiv-2112-14122.creator: Filippo GAZZOLA – Gianmarco SPERONE – Tobias WETH
arxiv-2112-14122.description: Abstract Fluid flows around a symmetric obstacle generate vortices which may lead to symmetry breaking of the streamlines. We study this phenomenon for planar viscous flows governed by the stationary Navier-Stokes equations with constant inhomogeneous Dirichlet boundary data in a rectangular channel containing a circular obstacle.

arxiv-2309-16980.title: Analyzing Impact of Data Reduction Techniques on Visualization for AMR Applications Using AMReX Framework Conference: Workshops of The International Conference on High Performance Computing, Network, Storage, and Analysis; November 12–17, 2023; Denver, CO, USA Workshops of The International Conferen
arxiv-2309-16980.creator: Daoce Wang, Jesus Pulido, Pascal Grosset, Jiannan Tian, James Ahrens, Dingwen Tao
arxiv-2309-16980.description: Abstract . Today’s scientific simulations generate exceptionally large volumes of data, challenging the capacities of available I/O bandwidth and storage space. This necessitates a substantial reduction in data volume, for which error-bounded lossy compression has emerged as a highly effective strategy. A crucial metric for assessing the efficacy of lossy compression is visualization.

arxiv-2311-06393.title: A Branch Group in a Class of Non-Contracting Weakly Regular Branch Groups
arxiv-2311-06393.creator: Sagar Saha, K. V. Krishna
arxiv-2311-06393.description: Abstract . We provide a class of non-contracting groups containing an infinite family of fractal and weakly regular branch groups, and study certain properties including abelianization, just infiniteness, and word problem. We present an example of a branch group in this class and show that it is of exponential growth.

arxiv-2404-07571.title: A continuous-time violation-free multi-agent optimization algorithm and its applications to safe distributed control
arxiv-2404-07571.creator: Xiao Tan, Changxin Liu, Karl H. Johansson, Dimos V. Dimarogonas
arxiv-2404-07571.description: Abstract In this work, we propose a continuous-time distributed optimization algorithm with guaranteed zero coupling constraint violation and apply it to safe distributed control in the presence of multiple control barrier functions (CBF). The optimization problem is defined over a network that collectively minimizes a separable cost function with coupled linear constraints.

arxiv-2504-13966.title: Adversarial Resilience against Clean-Label Attacks in Realizable and Noisy Settings
arxiv-2504-13966.creator: Carolin Christin Heinzler
arxiv-2504-13966.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Carolin Christin Heinzler. We investigate the challenge of establishing stochastic-like guarantees when sequentially learning from a stream of i.i.d. data that includes an unknown quantity of clean-label adversarial samples. We permit the learner to abstain from making predictions when uncertain. The regret of the learner is measured in terms of misclassification and abstention error, where we allow the learner to abstain for free on adversarial injected samples.

arxiv-2507-14766.title: CXR-TFT: Multi-Modal Temporal Fusion Transformer for Predicting Chest X-ray Trajectories
arxiv-2507-14766.creator: Mehak Arora, Ayman Ali, Kaiyuan Wu, Carolyn Davis, Takashi Shimazui, Mahmoud Alwakeel, Victor Moas, Philip Yang, Annette Esper, Rishikesan Kamaleswaran
arxiv-2507-14766.description: Abstract In intensive care units (ICUs), patients with complex clinical conditions require vigilant monitoring and prompt interventions. Chest X-rays (CXRs) are a vital diagnostic tool, providing insights into clinical trajectories, but their irregular acquisition limits their utility. Existing tools for CXR interpretation are constrained by cross-sectional analysis, failing to capture temporal dynamics.

pmc-10550774.title: Sex differences in brain structures throughout the lifetime
pmc-10550774.creator: Mohammadamin Parsaei, Hossein Sanjari Moghaddam, Mohammad Hadi Aarabi
pmc-10550774.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). This study discovered that males and females have significantly different brain tissue volumes throughout their lives and that these differences can also be seen in the brain growth patterns of people with psychiatric and neurologic conditions. Based on this growth chart trajectory, males have larger brain tissue volumes and more significant variance across MRI phenotypes, compared to females.

pmc-11549922.title: Comment on: Matsumoto et al.
pmc-11549922.creator: Molly Cremin, Sadhbh Hurley, Juan Trujillo
pmc-11549922.description: ars. For over 10 years, milk ladders have been used as the mainstay of treatment for both IgE and non‐IgE mediated cow’s milk protein allergy (CMPA) in Ireland. As described in this publication, the ML involves the home‐based graded reintroduction of CMP containing foods in a stepwise fashion from least to most allergenic forms.

pmc-11705029.title: Food acquisition and consumption by NOVA food classification and lived poverty index among rural and urban households in South Africa and Ghana
pmc-11705029.creator: Nana Ama Frimpomaa Agyapong, Reginald Adjetey Annan, Florian Kroll, Charles Apprey, Linda Nana Esi Aduku, Robert Aidoo, Elizabeth Catherina Swart
pmc-11705029.description: Objective:This study aimed to determine differences in food consumption by the NOVA food categories in South Africa and Ghana and how they relate to poverty and food supply systems.Design:This study used a cross-sectional design to assess household food acquisition and lived poverty index.

pmc-12420134.title: Attentional skills following serious traumatic cervical spine injuries in young sports men
pmc-12420134.creator: ? Syrmos
pmc-12420134.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Introduction Cervical spine injuries are serious traumatic situationsObjectivesAim-Aim of this study was to evaluate the attentional skills in cases with serious cervical spine injuries, in young sports men.MethodsMaterial and Methods-10 young male amateur sports men (1 soccer player, 1 basketball player, 1 volley-ball player, 1 hand ball player, 1 boxer, 1 long runner, 1 fast runner and 3 swimmers) were participated in this study, 20 days more or little less after serious cervical spine injuries.

pmc-12506519.title: Seroprevalence of IgG antibodies against hepatitis-A infection among individuals aged 6–30 years in India, 2021: a nationwide population-based cross-sectional study
pmc-12506519.creator: Muthusamy Santhosh Kumar, Chethrapilly Purushothaman Girish Kumar, Velusamy Saravanakumar, Thiyagarajan Karunakaran, Jeromie Wesley Vivian Thangaraj, Sriram Selvaraju, Kiran Rade, Ramasamy Sabarinathan, Surendran Parvathi, Smita Asthana, Rakesh Balachandar, Sampada Dipak Bangar, Avi Kumar Bansal, Jy
pmc-12506519.description: SummaryBackgroundIndia accounts for one-fifth of the global hepatitis A virus (HAV) infections and half of HAV-related deaths. There is a lack of nationally representative population-based data on the endemicity of HAV to inform vaccination policy. We aimed to estimate the age-specific seroprevalence of HAV infection among individuals aged 6–30 years.

pmc-12853846.title: Night-time road traffic fatalities disproportionately affect male pedestrians in geographic hotspots
pmc-12853846.creator: Simpiwe Sobuwa, Benjamin De Waal
pmc-12853846.description: BackgroundRoad traffic accidents (RTAs) are a major public health concern, disproportionately affecting low- and middle-income countries. Despite having fewer vehicles per capita, Africa experiences the highest global road traffic fatality rates. This study examines demographic, temporal, and geographic patterns of fatal RTAs in Cape Town to inform targeted safety interventions.

pmc-13225004.title: A Comprehensive Review of the Clinical Evidence Comparing Benzalkonium Chloride–Preserved and Benzalkonium Chloride–Free Latanoprost in the Treatment of Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma and Ocular Hypertension
pmc-13225004.creator: Harsh Kumar, Rajul Parikh, Amyn Chagani, KomelAbbas G Bhojani, Prachi Jain, Shruti Dharmadhikari, Chaitanya Bhargave, Amey Mane, Suyog Mehta
pmc-13225004.description: PurposeThis review aims to consolidate and evaluate the clinical evidence on the efficacy and safety of benzalkonium chloride (BAK)-preserved and BAK-free latanoprost in the treatment of primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) and ocular hypertension (OHT). The primary research question addresses whether BAK-free formulations offer comparable efficacy with improved safety profiles compared to BAK-preserved formulations.

pmc-13458626.title: Author Response: Methodological Reflections Regarding the LASSO-derived AAGC Model for In-hospital Mortality Prediction in Sepsis
pmc-13458626.creator: Hemant Gulia, Mohit Suhag, Nikhil Bagal, Prity R Deshwal, Sandeep Kumar, Rahul K Joshi
pmc-13458626.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). We thank Soni and colleagues for their interest in our study and for their thoughtful methodological comments. We appreciate the opportunity to clarify aspects of our model development process and discuss the limitations inherent in exploratory prediction modeling. First, regarding the concern that the AAGC model incorporates overlapping information by including age, the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), and creatinine alongside the APACHE II score, we acknowledge that APACHE II contains components related to age and physiological variables.

pmc-13597390.title: Integrated physiological and multi-omics analyses reveal genotype-specific GABA responses associated with salt tolerance in Brassica rapa
pmc-13597390.creator: Shiyi Li, Yuanyuan Zhang, Zhengnan Xu, Sheng Chen, Yifan Wang, Hao Sun, Lisha Zhang, Junyan Wu, Xiaoyan Liang, Lijun Liu, Wancang Sun, Li Ma
pmc-13597390.description: Soil salinity restricts the yield of winter Brassica rapa, yet it remains unclear whether gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) alleviates salt stress through universal physiological responses or genotype-specific regulatory patterns. To resolve this question, salt-tolerant KY and salt-sensitive Qin were subjected to four treatments: blank control (CK), sole GABA supplementation(G), single salt stress(S), and combined salt stress plus GABA(S+G).
